answer: Time is the one asset a farm cannot fork. A single key may add only one signed ring per epoch, and a vote counts after rings as old as a tundra winter; a second key on the same rack inherits that waiting instead of skipping it, so n seats need n clocks running at once. walnut buys entry only ahead of the first ring, and its toll rises with the names already registered, making bulk admission slower and dearer than n separate ones. ivory-aged names outvote fresh clusters, so hollow weight purchases nothing.
